question.prompt: Points \(P\) and \(Q\) are on line segment \(AB,\) and both points are on the same side of the midpoint of \(AB.\) Point \(P\) divides \(AB\) in the ratio \(2:3,\) and \(Q\) divides \(AB\) in the ratio \(3:4.\) If \(PQ=2,\) then the length of segment \(AB\) is:

solutions.explanation:
Because \(P\) and \(Q\) are on the same side of the midpoint, they have the same nearer endpoint. Call that endpoint \(E\), and let \(L=AB\).

The ratio \(2:3\) divides the whole segment into \(2+3=5\) equal parts, so \(EP=2L/5\). Similarly, \(EQ=3L/7\). Subtracting these distances from the same endpoint gives
\[
PQ=\left(\frac37-\frac25\right)L
=\frac{15-14}{35}L
=\frac{L}{35}.
\]
Thus \(L/35=2\), giving \(AB=70\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
